summary:
We developed Project KFC, an integrated web-based Moon Flight Simulator & CLPS Lunar Mission Browser designed to demonstrate how to plan and simulate direct-to-Earth (DTE) missions to the lunar south pole. 

Operating at the lunar south pole without relay satellites presents severe challenges, including prolonged darkness, extreme cold, and frequent Earth line-of-sight communication blackouts. KFC addresses this by uniting pre-launch mission configuration and real-time flight simulation into a single, easy-to-navigate browser interface. Users step through a guided workflow: selecting candidate landing sites (such as Malapert Massif or Haworth), configuring launch windows and historical reference rockets (including Saturn V, LVM3, and Long March 5), and verifying 6.5-day sunlight, thermal, and communication models against NASA Artemis and VIPER standards. Once all six pre-launch checks pass, users unlock the live flight console to simulate the full trajectory alongside real-time telemetry and an embedded NASA Eyes 3D visualization.
 
Project KFC is important because it turns complex orbital mechanics and NASA site-selection rules into a hands-on, visual walkthrough for students and mission planners.
details:
How does it work ? ( 2 stages )

Stage 1 :

- Users choose a candidate lunar south pole landing site, input terrain slope measurements, set a launch date/time, and select a reference launch vehicle.

- The engine samples 6.5 days of surface operations at 10-minute intervals to calculate sunlight availability, continuous darkness, Earth DTE line-of-sight windows, and surface thermal ranges.

Stage 2 :

- The browser evaluates the mission plan against six mandatory criteria modeled on NASA Artemis standards.

- Once all six checks pass -- the user unlocks the real-time flight console, users can simulate six flight phases. ( playback speeds up to 600,000× )

- It can complete with live engineering telemetry and an embedded NASA Eyes on the Solar System 3D viewer or other model.

The benefits of this Project KFC :

1.All-in-One Integrated Workflow -

Instead of switching between disconnected orbital calculators, static maps, and

spreadsheet checklists by uniting site comparison, it can launch scheduling, and

atrajectory playback in one web page.

2.Instant What-If Trade-Off Testing -

Changing any input — such as payload mass, launch date, or terrain slope —

immediately updates arrival schedules, thermal ranges, and pass/fail checks in real

time.

Impact of the Project :

- Democratizing Aerospace Mission Design

- Supporting STEM & Lunar Exploration Literacy

Tools, Coding Languages Hardware & Software

1. Coding Laguages : html, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+)

2. Tools : Eyes on the Solar System (NASA)

Our Project Creative ?

1. Pre-Launch Go -

Instead of letting users launch blindly, Project KFC enforces a realistic 6-Point NASA

Mission Gate that locks the launch button until the user engineers a valid landing site

and launch window.

2. Bridging Historical Rockets with Future CLPS Missions -

Creatively pairs historical flight timelines from four global space programs with

modern south pole robotic and crewed mission constraints.

The Factor our Team Consider :

1. No-Relay Communication Constraints -

Due toecause Earth hovers near the lunar horizon at south pole latitudes, our team

prioritized modeling Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight visibility and communication

blackout durations.

2. Solar Power & Thermal Survival -

Low sun elevation angles create long stretches of continuous darkness and extreme

cold; we factored in solar illumination percentages, maximum continuous darkness

hours, and thermal inertia swings over a 6.5-day surface window.

3. Model Transparency & Accessibility -

Explicitly documented model boundaries so users understand the difference

between educational simulation and flight-certified forecasting.
